task_2.title: Preserve lazy dask dataframe conversion for large datasets
task_2.description: The upgrade fixes a memory-heavy behavior in xarray when converting large datasets to a dask dataframe. `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` should remain lazy for dask-backed data instead of forcing large coordinate broadcasts into memory, which previously could crash notebooks or processes on sufficiently large inputs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that converting large dask-backed datasets to a dask dataframe remains lazy and does not crash or exhaust memory due to eager coordinate broadcasting.

expectation.grounded: When `xarray.Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` is called on datasets containing dask arrays and coordinate variables that need dimensional expansion, the conversion should preserve lazy dask semantics and avoid eager in-memory broadcasting of those coordinates. The returned object should still be a dask dataframe suitable for downstream lazy operations such as parquet writing.
expectation.conceptual: Converting a large lazily loaded dataset to a dask dataframe should behave as a lazy operation. Users should be able to continue working with or exporting the resulting dataframe without the conversion step unexpectedly materializing huge intermediate arrays in memory.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not change the public conversion entry point (`Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()`), must preserve compatibility with array backends that provide namespace-level broadcasting, and must avoid introducing eager materialization for coordinate expansion during dataframe conversion.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should reduce memory pressure without changing how users invoke the feature or weakening normal dataframe conversion behavior. Existing lazy workflows should continue to work, especially on large datasets that were previously unstable.

behavior: `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()` avoids eager broadcast-related memory allocation during conversion of large datasets.
Large dask-backed datasets that previously could crash a notebook or process during conversion should now produce a dask dataframe lazily.
Coordinate expansion needed for dataframe conversion should follow the active array backend's broadcasting behavior rather than relying on a NumPy-only eager broadcast path.
Downstream lazy dataframe workflows remain possible after conversion, including deferred export operations.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset contains large dask-backed variables and is converted with `Dataset.to_dask_dataframe()`, it should return a dask dataframe without forcing full in-memory realization of broadcasted coordinates.
When the same conversion is performed on datasets large enough to previously cause kernel or process failure from memory growth, it should complete without that eager-broadcast failure mode.
When the returned dask dataframe is used in a lazy downstream operation, the workflow should remain deferred rather than having been pre-materialized during conversion.
When coordinate variables require broadcasting for dataframe representation, the observable result should be a successful dataframe conversion with no regression in the user-facing API.

task_3.title: Preserve lazy behavior when reading xarray nbytes
task_3.description: Upgrading to xarray 2023.1.0 changes the observable behavior of `DataArray.nbytes` and `Variable.nbytes` so that byte-size inspection no longer triggers loading of the underlying array data. Users should be able to query memory size metadata for lazy or inaccessible array backends without materializing data, while still receiving an accurate byte count or a metadata-based estimate.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that checking the byte size of an xarray object does not accidentally load its underlying data into memory, especially for lazy, deferred, or otherwise inaccessible array backends.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.1.0, accessing `DataArray.nbytes` or `Variable.nbytes` must not force evaluation or loading of the wrapped array. The property should read byte-size information from the underlying stored array representation when available, and otherwise estimate the size from the object's `size` and `dtype`. This behavior must hold even when the backend array does not expose an `nbytes` attribute.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to inspect how many bytes an xarray object represents without that inspection causing data access, computation, or materialization. If exact byte metadata is unavailable, the library should still provide a sensible size estimate from known shape and data type information.

constraints.grounded: Accessing `DataArray.nbytes` and `Variable.nbytes` must remain side-effect free with respect to data loading. The returned value must stay consistent with the represented array size in bytes, including for arrays that omit an `nbytes` attribute but still provide enough metadata to compute the total. Existing lazy-array workflows must not fail merely because byte-size inspection occurs.
constraints.conceptual: Byte-size introspection should remain safe in lazy workflows, should not break deferred backends, and should continue to return an accurate or metadata-derived size rather than causing unexpected execution.

behavior: Reading `DataArray.nbytes` no longer materializes or loads deferred array data.
Reading `Variable.nbytes` no longer depends on access paths that can trigger backend loading.
When the underlying stored array exposes byte-size metadata, that metadata is used directly.
When direct byte-size metadata is absent, the reported size is derived from the array length and element size.
Arrays that are intentionally inaccessible unless loaded can still report `nbytes` successfully when shape and dtype metadata are available.
acceptance_criteria: When a `DataArray` wraps a lazy or inaccessible backend array, accessing `.nbytes` should return the correct byte count without loading the array.
When a `Variable` wraps a lazy or inaccessible backend array, accessing `.nbytes` should return the correct byte count without triggering backend evaluation.
When the wrapped backend does not define an `nbytes` attribute, `.nbytes` should still return a size derived from metadata if `size` and `dtype` are known.
When `.nbytes` is accessed during existing lazy workflows, it should not introduce new load-time errors that were previously unrelated to explicit data access.

task_1.title: Update CFTimeIndex lookup semantics for pandas 2.0 compatibility
task_1.description: The upgrade removes support for passing inexact-match lookup options through `CFTimeIndex.get_loc()`. Exact key lookup behavior remains available through `get_loc()`, while callers that previously relied on `method` or `tolerance` must use `CFTimeIndex.get_indexer()` for nearest, pad/backfill, or tolerance-bounded matching. This aligns the public behavior with newer pandas compatibility requirements.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2023.1.0 preserves exact `CFTimeIndex` key lookup through `get_loc()` while treating inexact matching as a separate indexer operation, so applications depending on nearest or tolerance-based lookup can migrate without ambiguity.

expectation.grounded: In 2023.1.0, `xarray.CFTimeIndex.get_loc()` accepts only a lookup key and no longer supports the `method` or `tolerance` keyword arguments. Exact lookups and string-based partial date slicing continue through `get_loc()`. Callers needing inexact matching semantics, including method-directed or tolerance-bounded resolution, are expected to use `CFTimeIndex.get_indexer([key], method=..., tolerance=...)` instead.
expectation.conceptual: Index location lookup should clearly separate exact matching from approximate matching. Exact key resolution should continue to work as before, but any lookup that depends on nearest-match behavior or a tolerance window should be performed through the API intended for indexer-based matching rather than through a single-key location helper.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade must not change observable exact-match `CFTimeIndex.get_loc()` results for valid keys, and string inputs should still support date-like slice resolution. The removed `method` and `tolerance` inputs must not be treated as supported `get_loc()` parameters in 2023.1.0. Inexact lookup behavior should remain available through `CFTimeIndex.get_indexer()`.
constraints.conceptual: Existing exact lookups and date-string slicing should remain stable, while only the calling convention for approximate lookup changes. The upgrade should not remove the ability to perform tolerant or nearest matching; it should only require those behaviors to be requested through the correct public interface.

behavior: `CFTimeIndex.get_loc()` performs exact key lookup only in 2023.1.0.
`CFTimeIndex.get_loc()` continues to support string inputs that resolve to date-based slices.
Approximate matching options formerly accepted by `get_loc()` are no longer part of that API surface.
Nearest, forward-fill, backfill, and tolerance-constrained lookup behavior should be requested via `CFTimeIndex.get_indexer()`.
The change is driven by compatibility with pandas 2.0 deprecation enforcement around index `get_loc()` semantics.
acceptance_criteria: When code calls `CFTimeIndex.get_loc(key)` with an exact key, it should continue to return the same location result as before the upgrade.
When code calls `CFTimeIndex.get_loc()` with a date-like string key, it should continue to provide the expected slice-style lookup behavior.
When code depends on nearest-match or tolerance-based lookup, it should obtain that result through `CFTimeIndex.get_indexer([key], method=..., tolerance=...)` rather than `get_loc()`.
When reviewing upgrade readiness, any use of `CFTimeIndex.get_loc(..., method=...)` or `CFTimeIndex.get_loc(..., tolerance=...)` should be treated as incompatible with 2023.1.0.
When migrating to 2023.1.0 alongside newer pandas versions, CFTimeIndex lookup behavior should remain functionally available without relying on deprecated `get_loc()` keyword arguments.

task_5.title: Add keep_attrs support to pad operations
task_5.description: The 2023.1.0 upgrade adds a `keep_attrs` parameter to xarray padding APIs so padding can preserve or drop metadata consistently. `Dataset.pad()`, `DataArray.pad()`, and `Variable.pad()` now expose explicit attribute-retention behavior, and when `keep_attrs` is not passed they follow the global xarray `keep_attrs` option instead of silently discarding attrs during pad operations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that padding a Dataset, DataArray, or Variable can preserve metadata when requested, and that pad operations no longer silently drop attrs when users rely on `keep_attrs` semantics.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.Dataset.pad()`, `xarray.DataArray.pad()`, and `xarray.Variable.pad()` must accept a `keep_attrs` parameter. When `keep_attrs=True`, the returned object must retain the source object's `attrs`; when `keep_attrs=False`, the returned object must be returned without attrs. When `keep_attrs=None` or omitted, pad behavior must follow the active xarray `keep_attrs` option. For Dataset and DataArray padding, the same retention behavior must apply to padded coordinates and padded variables involved in the result, while unaffected members remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Padding APIs should give users explicit, reliable control over whether metadata is preserved. If metadata preservation is enabled directly or through the library's default attribute policy, the padded result should keep its attrs; if disabled, the padded result should omit them. This behavior should be consistent across dataset, array, variable, and padded coordinate outputs.

constraints.grounded: Padding semantics, shapes, coordinate values, and non-padded members must remain unchanged apart from the documented attribute-retention behavior. Omitting `keep_attrs` must remain valid and must defer to the configured global `keep_attrs` option rather than requiring callers to pass the parameter explicitly.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must only change observable metadata retention behavior for padding and must not alter the actual padded data result or require callers to change existing pad usage unless they want different metadata handling.

behavior: `Dataset.pad()` now exposes `keep_attrs` as a public parameter controlling whether dataset-level attrs are preserved in the padded result.
`DataArray.pad()` now exposes `keep_attrs` as a public parameter controlling whether data array attrs are preserved in the padded result.
`Variable.pad()` now exposes `keep_attrs` as a public parameter controlling whether variable attrs are preserved in the padded result.
When `keep_attrs` is omitted or `None`, pad operations use the active global xarray `keep_attrs` setting as the default behavior.
When padding introduces new coordinate values, padded coordinates retain or drop attrs in line with the resolved `keep_attrs` behavior.
In `Dataset.pad()`, variables and coordinates not affected by the requested padding remain unchanged, including their existing attrs.
acceptance_criteria: When a `DataArray` with attrs is padded with `keep_attrs=True`, the returned padded array and any padded coordinates should preserve their attrs.
When a `DataArray` with attrs is padded with `keep_attrs=False`, the returned padded array and any padded coordinates should not expose those attrs.
When a `Variable` with attrs is padded with `keep_attrs=True`, the returned variable should preserve its attrs.
When a `Variable` with attrs is padded with `keep_attrs=False`, the returned variable should not preserve its attrs.
When a `Dataset` with attrs is padded along one dimension with `keep_attrs=True`, dataset attrs and attrs on padded variables and padded coordinates should be preserved.

When a `Dataset` with attrs is padded along one dimension with `keep_attrs=False`, dataset attrs and attrs on padded variables and padded coordinates should be absent, while non-padded dataset members should remain otherwise unchanged.
When `keep_attrs` is not passed to any supported pad API, the result should match the active global `keep_attrs` option setting.

task_6.title: Optimize alignment when indexed and non-indexed objects already match
task_6.description: The upgrade improves xarray alignment performance for operations that combine indexed and non-indexed objects with the same shape, especially Dataset assignment. It avoids unnecessary reindexing when indexes already match or when unindexed dimensions have compatible sizes, while preserving reindexing when indexes differ or dimension sizes are inconsistent.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that alignment-heavy operations such as assigning a DataArray into a Dataset do not incur unnecessary reindexing when indexed and non-indexed inputs already have compatible dimensions and equivalent indexes, while still reindexing whenever indexes or dimension sizes are not truly compatible.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.1.0, alignment and assignment logic should treat identical index objects as already equal, and should avoid reindexing when indexed and non-indexed operands have matching dimension sizes for the aligned dimensions. Operations such as Dataset.assign with a non-indexed DataArray of the same dimension length, or with a variable backed by the same index object, should complete without the previous alignment slowdown. Reindexing should still occur when compared indexes are unequal, when multiple conflicting unindexed sizes are present for a dimension, or when an unindexed dimension size does not match the size implied by indexed variables.
expectation.conceptual: Operations that combine labeled and unlabeled data of the same shape should remain fast when no actual alignment work is needed. The library should recognize when coordinates already match or when only compatible dimension lengths need to be checked, and it should preserve existing alignment behavior for mismatched indexes or incompatible sizes.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable alignment outcome for unequal indexes or incompatible dimension sizes. Alignment must continue to reindex when compared indexes are not equal, when an unindexed dimension appears with more than one distinct size across inputs, or when an unindexed dimension size disagrees with the corresponding indexed dimension size. Equal-by-identity indexes must be accepted as equal without extra comparison overhead.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must not weaken correctness checks. Cases that genuinely need alignment should still be aligned, and only redundant work should be removed.

behavior: Alignment short-circuits index comparison when all compared indexes are the same object.
Assignment or alignment between indexed and non-indexed objects with the same dimension size avoids unnecessary reindexing.
Reindexing still happens when aligned indexes are not equal.
Reindexing still happens when unindexed inputs imply conflicting sizes for the same dimension.
Reindexing still happens when an unindexed dimension size does not match the corresponding indexed dimension size.
The main user-visible effect is improved runtime for compatible alignment and Dataset.assign scenarios, without changing successful results for already compatible inputs.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset is assigned a non-indexed DataArray whose dimension length matches the Dataset's indexed dimension, the assignment should complete without an avoidable alignment slowdown and should preserve the expected result.
When an operation aligns objects that share the exact same index object, it should treat those indexes as equal and avoid redundant index comparison or reindexing work.
When aligned objects have unequal indexes, the operation should still perform reindexing as required by xarray alignment semantics.
When multiple unindexed operands provide different sizes for the same aligned dimension, the operation should not skip reindexing.
When an unindexed operand's dimension size differs from the corresponding indexed dimension size, the operation should not skip reindexing.
For compatible indexed and non-indexed inputs, upgrading to 2023.1.0 should improve performance relative to the regressed 2022.12.0 behavior while keeping observable data results unchanged.

task_4.title: Preserve xr.where usability with NumPy inputs when keep_attrs is enabled
task_4.description: The update fixes a regression in xarray 2022.12.0 where `xr.where()` could fail when attribute preservation was enabled and the inputs were plain NumPy values or arrays. In 2023.1.0, NumPy-only calls continue to work under `keep_attrs=True`, while xarray objects still retain their expected attribute behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `xr.where()` works correctly when attribute preservation is enabled, including cases where the operands are plain NumPy scalars or arrays rather than xarray objects.

expectation.grounded: When `xr.where(..., keep_attrs=True)` is called with inputs that produce a non-xarray result, such as NumPy scalars or `numpy.ndarray` values, it should return the computed NumPy result without raising an `AttributeError` related to missing `attrs`. When the result is an xarray object that supports `attrs`, existing `keep_attrs` behavior should still apply, including propagating attributes from `x` and handling Dataset promotion cases consistently.
expectation.conceptual: Attribute preservation in `xr.where()` should only affect results that actually support attributes. Calls that operate purely on NumPy data should still succeed and return the expected value, while xarray results should continue to preserve metadata in the same user-visible way as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing `keep_attrs=True` behavior for `DataArray`, `Dataset`, or other xarray results with `attrs`. NumPy-only results must not gain fabricated metadata or change result type solely because attribute preservation was requested.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be limited to preventing failures on metadata-free results. It should not alter normal metadata propagation for labeled xarray objects, and it should not introduce new metadata or wrapper objects for plain NumPy outputs.

behavior: `xr.where(..., keep_attrs=True)` no longer fails when the computed result is a plain NumPy scalar or array without an `attrs` attribute.
NumPy-only `xr.where()` calls continue to return the expected NumPy value or array even when global or explicit attribute preservation is enabled.
For xarray results that expose `attrs`, `keep_attrs=True` continues to preserve attributes from `x` as part of the existing metadata behavior.
Special handling for Dataset-producing cases remains intact when `y` is a `Dataset` and `x` is not a `Dataset`.
acceptance_criteria: When attribute preservation is enabled and `xr.where(True, 0, 1, keep_attrs=True)` is evaluated, it should return the NumPy result for the true branch and should not raise an exception.
When attribute preservation is enabled globally and `xr.where()` is called with NumPy arrays only, it should complete successfully and return the correct NumPy output.
When `xr.where()` returns a `DataArray` or `Dataset` and `keep_attrs=True`, it should continue to preserve the source metadata according to existing xarray behavior.

When a mixed input case promotes the result to a `Dataset`, metadata handling should remain consistent with prior documented `xr.where()` semantics rather than regressing because of the NumPy-input fix.

task_7.title: Preserve coordinate dtypes when accessing stacked MultiIndex levels
task_7.description: Upgrading to 2023.1.0 fixes an xarray regression where coordinates used to build a stacked MultiIndex could be returned with widened dtypes when accessed afterward. The update preserves the original coordinate dtype for MultiIndex level access so stacked datasets expose the same logical value types users created.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that stacking coordinates into a MultiIndex does not change the user-observed dtype of the original coordinate when that coordinate is accessed afterward.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.1.0, coordinates retrieved from a stacked MultiIndex-backed Dataset or DataArray should preserve the original dtype of the source index level. Accessing a coordinate created from values such as int32 or float32 through MultiIndex level access should return arrays with the same dtype rather than a widened dtype.
expectation.conceptual: Users should observe the same value type before and after stacking coordinates into a MultiIndex. Creating or reading stacked coordinates should not silently promote numeric types.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing MultiIndex access behavior while preventing implicit dtype widening during array conversion of individual index levels. Non-level MultiIndex array access should continue to behave as before, and supported numeric dtypes should round-trip without changing their public dtype.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove unintended type changes and must not alter the normal semantics of stacked indexing. Existing workflows that read stacked coordinates should keep working, except that returned dtypes now remain stable.

behavior: When a coordinate is used to create a stacked MultiIndex, accessing that coordinate afterward returns values with the original dtype.
Numeric dtypes that were previously widened during MultiIndex level access, including 32-bit integer and 32-bit floating-point values, now remain unchanged.
The observable effect is on returned array dtype, not on the coordinate values themselves.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset coordinate of dtype int32 is stacked into a MultiIndex and then accessed, it should still report dtype int32.
When a Dataset coordinate of dtype float32 is stacked into a MultiIndex and then accessed, it should still report dtype float32.
When users compare a coordinate dtype before stacking and after accessing the stacked coordinate, the dtypes should match for supported preserved numeric types.
When interacting with stacked coordinates, the upgrade should not require users to manually cast values back to the original dtype.

task_8.title: Normalize xarray package imports to absolute module paths
task_8.description: The 2023.1.0 update standardizes xarray's internal and test-suite imports to use absolute `xarray...` module paths instead of package-relative imports. This is intended to improve maintainability and tooling compatibility without changing the library's user-facing data model or core API behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2023.1.0 preserves existing xarray behavior while the package adopts absolute import paths throughout the library and associated test helpers.

expectation.grounded: xarray should continue to expose the same public top-level APIs from `xarray`, including core objects such as `DataArray`, `Dataset`, `Variable`, backend open/load helpers, plotting accessors, calendar/time utilities, merge/combine helpers, and configuration helpers, while internal modules resolve dependencies through absolute imports like `xarray.core.*`, `xarray.backends.*`, `xarray.coding.*`, `xarray.plot.*`, and `xarray.tests.*` rather than relative imports.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, users should observe the same importable xarray functionality and package behavior as before. The main change is that the project now consistently resolves modules through full package-qualified imports, improving package consistency without introducing a new user-facing feature.

constraints.grounded: The import normalization must not change the public names exported from `xarray`, must not alter the observable behavior of dataset, data array, backend, plotting, calendar, indexing, interpolation, concat, merge, weighted, rolling, or accessor functionality, and must not introduce new warnings or exceptions solely because modules are imported through absolute package paths. Existing test support imports via `xarray.tests` and referenced test modules should remain importable.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be behavior-preserving. Existing workflows, imports, and runtime results should remain stable, and users should not need to change how they call xarray APIs just because the package's internal import style changed.

behavior: Importing `xarray` should continue to make the same top-level public API available as in the previous version.
Core library modules should resolve one another through absolute `xarray...` package paths instead of relative imports.
Backend, coding, plotting, indexing, computation, merge, concat, rolling, accessor, and calendar-related modules should remain importable and functionally unchanged from a user perspective.
Test utilities and cross-test imports should resolve via `xarray.tests` and absolute test module paths without depending on relative-import layout.
Observable library behavior should remain stable; the upgrade primarily affects package organization and import resolution semantics rather than feature output.
acceptance_criteria: When a user imports `xarray`, it should continue to expose the expected public objects and helper functions available before the upgrade.
When code imports core xarray submodules through their package-qualified names, the imports should succeed without requiring relative-import context.

When users run existing xarray workflows involving datasets, data arrays, backends, plotting, interpolation, indexing, concat, merge, and time/calendar utilities, the observable results should remain unchanged by this upgrade.
When downstream tests or tooling import xarray test helpers through `xarray.tests` or package-qualified test modules, those imports should resolve successfully.
When the library is imported under normal package usage, it should not raise new import-related warnings or errors that are attributable only to the absolute-import conversion.
